about: pass 4 notes: pass 2's, with D02, D04 and D05 revised after the two pass 4 recuts, and pass 4's Part A return

D01.outside: Asking another room, as a room, for help (Reciprocity, in Order without law); near case: a room asking its neighbour to defend its flag, hands sought from a room rather than from members.
D01.least_sure: T4-003 Sensemaking: teaching newcomers what the canvas is and how to place adds hands (inside), but much of it is interpretation of the event in general (outside).

D02.outside: Calling hands (Mobilization, in Critical mass); claiming the nation beyond the mark (Flagging the nation, in Collective identity); near case: a call that brings placers but says nothing about what or where to place.
D02.least_sure: T4-006 Collective representation: choosing the emblem settles what the room acts on (inside), but it is argued as what the room is (Collective identity); from pass 4 it holds the land's flag and emblems.

D03.outside: Moving after the spot is lost (relocation, in Order without law); near case: day9 leaving Norway's border to rebuild elsewhere, giving up the old work rather than keeping it.
D03.least_sure: T4-019 Attribution: reading a change decides how the work is kept (inside), but it is also the hinge between restraint and contention toward a neighbour (Order without law).

D04.outside: Moves against a rival and talk with a rival (D08 Contention); canvas-born colour factions (Neo-tribes, in Collective identity); near case: the void, a body of individual placers rather than a room acting toward rooms.
D04.least_sure: T4-014 Territoriality, widened at pass 4: a room's claim on space (inside), and with hosting a rule over guests' works on its mark, which could read as one relation with each guest (Reciprocity).

D05.outside: Choosing the emblem, the land's flag and emblems included from pass 4 (Collective representation, in Coordination without command); near case: a fandom room arguing which character to draw, a choice inside a membership rather than the membership itself.
D05.least_sure: T4-004 Frame bridging: the room's culture carried onto the canvas is membership (inside), or interpretation of the event (Sensemaking).

D06.outside: Explaining what the canvas is (Sensemaking, in Critical mass); near case: a member explaining the event to a confused reader, which makes sense of it rather than framing the host space.
D06.least_sure: T4-002 Boundary work: a line drawn around the host space (inside), or the community deciding the canvas work's standing in its name (Collective identity).

D07.outside: Screenshots shared during the work to coordinate repair (Repair work, in Maintenance); near case: a member posting the current state of the logo at h40 to call for fixes, a record used to keep the work rather than left after it.
D07.least_sure: T4-025 Visibility returns: what being seen leaves in the community (inside), or a way of bringing hands (Critical mass).

D08.outside: Restraint toward a neighbour, deals and truces (D04 Order without law): an attack call refused or met with a truce passes there; near case: members reining in their own room's attackers (Live and let live).
D08.least_sure: T4-021 Rivalry: talk carried on with a rival during and after a contest (inside), or an identity built against an out-group (Collective identity).

pairs.D01|D02: Critical mass asks whether there are hands; Coordination without command asks how hands already there are aligned on one picture.
pairs.D01|D03: Critical mass gathers hands to make a work; Maintenance keeps a made work with the hands it has.
pairs.D01|D04: Critical mass looks inward at the room's own numbers; Order without law looks across at other rooms.
pairs.D01|D05: Critical mass counts hands; Collective identity says whose hands they are and what membership they carry.
pairs.D01|D06: Critical mass concerns the hands for the canvas work; Host framing concerns the host community's terms for talking about it.
pairs.D01|D07: Critical mass comes before a work exists; Imprinting is what a work leaves after the clock.
pairs.D02|D03: Coordination without command aligns placers to make the picture; Maintenance keeps it against erosion once it stands.
pairs.D02|D04: Coordination without command works inside a room; Order without law works between rooms.
pairs.D02|D05: Coordination without command settles what the room makes and how; Collective identity is the membership that can make a choice obvious before any coordination.
pairs.D02|D06: Coordination without command aligns the canvas work; Host framing sets where and in what frame the community talks about it.
pairs.D02|D07: Coordination without command makes the work; Imprinting carries something of it beyond the clock.
pairs.D03|D04: Maintenance keeps the work against any erosion and reads changes to it; Order without law deals with the neighbour as a room.
pairs.D03|D05: Maintenance is about keeping a thing; Collective identity is about who keeps it and why it matters to them.
pairs.D03|D06: Maintenance acts on the canvas; Host framing acts on the community's own space.
pairs.D03|D07: Maintenance keeps the work during the clock; Imprinting keeps something of it after.
pairs.D04|D05: Order without law is the relation between rooms; Collective identity is the membership a room or tribe carries, even where that membership shapes its relations.
pairs.D04|D06: Order without law is made between rooms on the canvas; Host framing is made inside one community's own space.
pairs.D04|D07: Order without law holds during the work; Imprinting is what the community keeps after.
pairs.D05|D06: Collective identity is the membership the work carries; Host framing is the frame laid over the community's space during the event.
pairs.D05|D07: Collective identity is carried into the work; Imprinting is what the work leaves in the community afterwards, emblems included.
pairs.D06|D07: Host framing is the community's reception of the event at its start; Imprinting is what stays at its end.
pairs.D01|D08: Critical mass gathers hands for the room's own work; Contention turns hands against a rival's work.
pairs.D02|D08: Coordination without command aligns placers on the room's own picture; Contention aims them at another room's.
pairs.D03|D08: Maintenance keeps a work against any erosion; Contention is the erosion a room aims at another, and the talk around it.
pairs.D04|D08: Order without law is how rooms hold, spare, trade, settle and federate; Contention is how a room wages a contest. An attack call refused, or met with a truce, passes from the second into the first.
pairs.D05|D08: Collective identity is the membership a room carries; Contention is a contest with a named rival, whether or not the rivalry comes from that membership.
pairs.D06|D08: Host framing is the community's frame on its own space; Contention is acted on the canvas against another room.
pairs.D07|D08: Imprinting is what a work leaves after the clock; Contention is fought during it, though victory claims and salutes cross hour 73.

gates.all: every room of the analysed set: the canvas and April Fools reached every sub, and nothing the record shows kept a room from doing this
gates.work: the room had a work of its own on the canvas by its own record: it carries a build, extension, personal-piece, announcement, found-mark or celebration theme (T3-038, T3-041, T3-060, T3-026, T3-082, T3-009)
gates.other: the room names another subreddit in its coded record (rooms.jsonl n_subreddits_named > 0, through mem.py facts): it had another room in view
gates.after: the room has a coded turn after hour 73 (rooms.jsonl onset_last_code_hour > 73): it was still writing when the work could only be kept or carried on
gates.apr1: the room has a coded turn before hour 32, the end of 1 April UTC (rooms.jsonl onset_first_code_hour < 32): it was writing on the day a play frame could be laid

least_sure_dims.text: D05 Collective identity and D02 Coordination without command**, now that the land's flag and emblems cross from the first to the second (pass 4)

return.alternative: The reviewer's partition (C2c), adjusted Rand 0.661 against mine. Two of its divergences were taken at pass 4 as recuts by rules written first: hosting beside territory, and the land's flag and emblems beside the mark's content. Three were refused: relocation joined to collective efficacy (it would hide the order the move arrow claims), reconciliation apart from restraint (both answer how a room keeps from harming another's work) and identity split by activity (membership must stay a construct the return can test); the last stands beside the claim. The host sub split by actor was run as a test, not a recut: both actors' acts follow the calls.
return.least_sure_t4: T4-022 Flagging the nation.** After the flag and emblems left it, it holds the nation claimed beyond the mark, and its one test (membership carried in before the attack, on the narrowed candidate) came out below the null mean. Next to it, T4-007 Stigmergy, which rests on two large themes.
